capability: Deterministic constraint envelope evaluation for two-part coating formulations. For every (candidate mass, policy envelope) pair, `evaluate_envelope_policy` computes per-constraint margins and a single `pass_all_hard` decision under inclusive f64 bounds. Phase-0 covers mass-only feature paths ({mass.part_A_g, mass.part_B_g, mass.total_g}); Phase-1 will extend to `volume.*`, `voc.*`, `solids_content.*` once ingredient-library rights are cleared and the dimensioned-arithmetic FeatureSnapshot is signed.
population: Ten published two-part epoxy-amine coating formulation envelopes spanning aliphatic polyamine (TETA/DETA/TEPA), cycloaliphatic amine (IPDA/PACM), aromatic amine (MXDA/MPDA), amidoamine adduct, and Mannich-base families. Fifty labelled test cases: NOMINAL, AT_LOWER_BOUNDARY, AT_UPPER_BOUNDARY, JUST_BELOW_LOWER, WILDLY_OUT. Envelope tolerances are ±5 percent by mass per part, cited from Wicks/Jones/Pappas 2007 §24.3 typical coating industry QC bands and supplier TDS 'mix within ±5%' quotes; total tolerance follows additive propagation.
split_methodology: No fitting — envelope evaluation is deterministic constraint satisfaction. Each envelope carries an explicit policy JSON and a set of trusted arithmetic snapshots forming a five-category test grid. Boundary cases are constructed so the runtime computes `margin.to_bits() == 0.0_f64.to_bits()` exactly, exercising INCLUSIVE_BOUNDARY_DRIFT.
theory: Constraint envelope QC (Wicks, Jones & Pappas 'Organic Coatings: Science and Technology' 4th ed. 2007 Chapter 24 'Quality Control', §24.3 mixing tolerances; Ellis 'Chemistry and Technology of Epoxy Resins' 1993 Chapter 6 formulation ratio recommendations). Every commercial two-part coating specification includes a mixing envelope `nominal ± tolerance` on part masses (or mass ratio) with additive tolerance propagation onto total mass. A batch is in-spec iff every published constraint's actual value falls within its inclusive bounds. The runtime's per-constraint margin `min(v - lower, upper - v)` gives both pass/fail and how-close-to-boundary diagnostic for QC operators.

metrics.name: envelope_gate_correctness_rate
metrics.note: Fraction of the 10-envelope × 5-case fixture where evaluate_envelope_policy(...).pass_all_hard matches the expected label. Ten envelopes × 30 expected-pass cases + 20 expected-fail cases.

metrics.name: inclusive_boundary_correctness_rate
metrics.note: INCLUSIVE_BOUNDARY_DRIFT axis. Ten AT_LOWER + 10 AT_UPPER = 20 at-boundary cases assert margin.to_bits() == 0.0_f64.to_bits() and pass_all_hard=true; 10 JUST_BELOW_LOWER cases assert margin<0 and pass_all_hard=false. All 30 boundary-adjacent cases verified.

metrics.name: envelope_policy_substitution_fail_closed_rate
metrics.note: ENVELOPE_POLICY_SUBSTITUTION axis. Seven probes covering wrong schema, empty policy_id, non-authoritative + allow_synthetic_fixture=false, non-authoritative + fixture_only=false, empty constraints, duplicate constraint_ids, unknown feature_path all return ABSTAIN status or Err.

metrics.name: trusted_feature_substitution_fail_closed_rate
metrics.note: TRUSTED_FEATURE_SUBSTITUTION axis. Five probes: wrong snapshot schema, snapshot.trusted=false, missing feature, non-finite snapshot value, unit mismatch (kg vs g). All fail closed.

metrics.name: envelope_bound_inversion_fail_closed_rate
metrics.note: ENVELOPE_BOUND_INVERSION axis. Three probes: lower > upper, lower = NaN, upper = Infinity. All return Err.

metrics.name: candidate_gate_pass_injection_ignore_rate
metrics.note: CANDIDATE_GATE_PASS_INJECTION axis. Two directional probes: candidate authors JSON claiming pass_all_hard=true when snapshot is out-of-envelope, and pass_all_hard=false when snapshot is in-envelope. In both, the runtime's authoritative evaluation overrides the candidate's assertion. The runtime is the sole producer of EnvelopeGateResultV1; candidate injections are ignored.

metrics.name: authority_lock_preservation_rate
metrics.note: Every fixture output preserves ranking_eligible=false, usable_by_optimizer=false, authority_upgrade=false, wet_lab_evidence_created=false, qualification_evidence_created=false, release_evidence_created=false, product_evidence_created=false, objective_values={}. Runtime cannot upgrade authority under any policy or snapshot.

metrics.name: minimum_positive_margin_g
metrics.note: Observational. Zero because at-boundary test cases construct margin=0.0 exactly (INCLUSIVE_BOUNDARY_DRIFT axis assertion).

metrics.name: worst_case_negative_margin_g
metrics.note: Observational. WILDLY_OUT test cases place part_A at 2× upper bound; the worst observed negative margin was -210 g on the PACM marine-topcoat envelope where nominal 200 g × 2 = 400 g exceeds the 210 g upper by 190 g and the pattern in WILDLY_OUT cases pushes ~-210 g on the tightest envelope.

fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.prediction_rule: For each constraint c in policy: margin[c.constraint_id] = min(snapshot.values[c.feature_path].value - c.lower_inclusive, c.upper_inclusive - snapshot.values[c.feature_path].value). pass_all_hard = ∀c: margin[c] >= 0.
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.policy_trust_rule: policy_trusted = policy.authoritative OR (allow_synthetic_fixture AND policy.fixture_only AND NOT policy.authoritative)
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.boundary_semantics: inclusive on both ends; margin=0 at boundary → pass
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.note: There is no meaningful baseline because constraint satisfaction is arithmetic, not modelling. The KPI compares runtime output to labeled expected pass/fail from published envelopes.
